title: Samantabhadra
hookLine: the bodhisattva of practice and great vows

lines: WHEN SPACE ENDS, THE VOW ENDS.
cards: When space itself comes to an end, my vow will come to an end. But space never ends, so neither will the vow.

That, in paraphrase, is the refrain at the close of a vast Mahayana sutra, and the one speaking it is a bodhisattva named Samantabhadra. A promise with no expiry date. Not a resolution that fades by February.
A vow as wide as the sky, repeated until it sinks in.

teach.h: A LION AND A WHITE ELEPHANT.
teach.b: First, the pair. In some Chinese temples the Buddha sits with a bodhisattva on either side: Manjushri on a lion, and Samantabhadra on a white elephant. Wisdom and practice, side by side.
The elephant suits practice: slow, steady, very hard to push off the road.

teach.h: VOWS THAT LAST AS LONG AS SPACE.
teach.b: Second, the vows. The Flower Ornament Sutra, the Avatamsaka, ends with Samantabhadra setting out his great vows.

teach.h: REJOICE IN THE GOOD OF OTHERS.
teach.b: In paraphrase: to honor all the Buddhas; to praise them; to make offerings; to admit and turn from the harm one has done; to rejoice in the good done by others; to ask the Buddhas to teach; to ask them to stay in the world; to follow their example; to meet every being where they are; and to give away the merit of everything, for the good of all.

teach.h: HE COMES TO THOSE WHO PRACTICE.
teach.b: After each comes the same refrain about space and its endlessness. Third, the small one in the big list: the fifth, rejoicing in the good done by others.

Being glad when a coworker gets the praise, or a sister's life goes better than yours. In the sutra it stands right beside honoring all the Buddhas, with the same endless vow. Practice includes the small, daily kinds.

In the last chapter of the Lotus Sutra, Samantabhadra arrives from far away and promises that whoever keeps and studies that sutra, he will come to them on his white elephant, to guard them and to teach them again any line they've forgotten.
Practice, in that promise, is never quite done alone.

how: In East Asian Buddhism the vows of Samantabhadra are recited in temples and at home, and Samantabhadra is shown on a white elephant, often beside Manjushri on his lion.

o: the bodhisattva of practice, whose vows last as long as space
a Chinese emperor who built great temples for the Buddha
the white elephant seen in the dream of the Buddha's mother

s: Samantabhadra's vows end when the work is finished
the refrain: when space ends, the vow ends, and space never ends.
one of the vows is to rejoice in the good done by others
it stands beside honoring all the Buddhas, with the same endless refrain.
in the Lotus Sutra, Samantabhadra promises to guard those who keep the sutra
he says he'll come to them on his white elephant.

games.q: you've taken on the vow to rejoice in the good done by others. then a friend lands the very thing you were hoping for. what does the vow ask?
o: wait to be glad until you get yours too
say nothing, so it stays even
games.why: rejoicing in others' good is one of Samantabhadra's great vows, and in the sutra it gets the same endless refrain as honoring the Buddhas.

practice: Choose one small practice you could actually keep: a minute of quiet before picking up the phone, a kind word to someone you usually rush past, being glad out loud when someone else does well.
Then, silently and in your own words, make it a vow, not until space ends, just today, and then today again. Rest with it, the way the elephant stands: steady, unhurried.

wordCard.voice: Samantabhadra. The bodhisattva of practice and great vows, riding a white elephant, whose vows last as long as space. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the name of the bodhisattva of practice, called Puxian in China and Fugen in Japan.

carryVoice: Your line: great vows. As wide as space, and kept one day at a time. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Avatamsaka Sutra, the Practices and Vows of Samantabhadra (closing chapter of the Gandavyuha)
Lotus Sutra, final chapter (the encouragement of Samantabhadra)
